proof_summary: Assume either prime family is finite and choose \(N\ge5\) bounding the relevant prime (enlarged by 2 for the upper member of a twin pair); applying the hypothesis to \((N+1)!/6\) yields primes \(p=6x-1\) and \(q=6y+1\) with \((N+1)!=p+q\). The bounded summand divides the factorial and therefore the other prime, forcing \(p=q\), so \((N+1)!\le2N\), contradicting \((N+1)!>2N\).
